data.title: PowerCell receives SEK 440 million order for utility-scale green hydrogen power generation installation in the US
data.description:
PowerCell Group has, through its U.S. subsidiary PowerCell Inc., signed an agreement worth SEK 440 million with an established U.S.-based electric cooperative for a utility-scale fuel cell installation in the southern United States. Based on PowerCell's containerized PowerPod 3000 platform, the installation will comprise 27 MW of installed fuel cell capacity and deliver 20 MW of rated power. Delivery is expected over 18–24 months.

The installation will form part of the customer's renewable energy system, where excess solar-generated electricity is used to produce green hydrogen for long-duration energy storage. The stored hydrogen can then be converted back into electricity through PowerCell's PEM fuel cells at night, during periods of low solar generation, or when additional power is needed.

By extending the availability of solar energy beyond the hours of generation, the system increases the utilization and value of the customer's renewable energy assets while providing dispatchable power when needed.

The fuel cell installation will also generate water as part of the electrochemical conversion of hydrogen into electricity. This creates an opportunity to recover and reuse water within the broader energy system, potentially reducing its net water requirements. In regions where water availability is an important consideration, the ability to generate both electricity and recoverable water adds another dimension of value to hydrogen-based energy storage. The amount of water recovered, and its potential uses will depend on the final system configuration, operating conditions and water treatment requirements.

Industrialized technology for utility-scale power generation

PowerCell will supply and integrate the fuel cell power generation installation within its agreed scope, converting green hydrogen from the customer's energy storage system into electricity. The parties also intend to enter into a dedicated service level agreement prior to commissioning.

The installation is based on PowerCell's PowerPod 3000, a containerized power generation platform integrating our PS190 systems with power conversion equipment, cooling and DMC, PowerCell's control and Energy Orchestration technology.

The modular architecture combines 27 MW of installed fuel cell capacity with 20 MW of rated power, providing a scalable platform designed for high availability, operational flexibility and efficient utilization of the fuel cell systems. The project demonstrates how hydrogen can complement other energy storage technologies by storing excess renewable energy over longer periods and making it available when generation and demand do not coincide. The integration of renewable generation, hydrogen storage, dispatchable electricity and water recovery illustrates the potential for more resilient and resource-efficient energy systems.

Establishing Power Generation as a major growth segment

"For PowerCell, this order represents an important step in establishing Power Generation as our second major segment alongside Marine. It demonstrates how our industrialized PEM technology, system integration and Energy Orchestration capabilities can create value at utility scale. What makes this application particularly interesting is the combination of energy and water. Our fuel cells convert stored hydrogen into reliable electricity while also producing water that can potentially be recovered and reused. In regions where both energy resilience and water availability matter, we see significant value in designing systems that make better use of both resources. This is the direction we are taking PowerCell: creating greater customer value by integrating our technology into complete energy solutions," says Richard Berkling, CEO of PowerCell Group.

PowerCell is a world leader in hydrogen electric solutions with unique fuel cell stacks and systems. A presentation featuring CEO Richard Paxman commenting on the interim report, followed by a Q&A session moderated by Maria Karlsson Osipova of DNB Carnegie, will be available at 9:00 a.m. CET here: https://www.youtube.com/@DNBCarnegiePlay

Significant Events

During

Paxman announced a series of significant regulatory milestones on the 14th July, supporting the forthcoming commercialisation of its device to prevent chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy. Paxman has successfully extended the scope of its UK Conformity Assessed (UKCA), European Conformity (CE), International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 13485 and Medical Device Single Audit Program (MDSAP) certifications to include its new cryocompression technology for the management of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN).

The extended scope fulfils certification requirements in the UK and the EU and represent a key milestone toward approvals in Australia, Brazil, Canada, Japan and the United States.

On July 16th, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has released its Calendar Year (CY) 2027 proposed Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) rules affecting mechanical scalp cooling. The proposed OPPS rule would establish separate payment for CPT® code 97008, following continued dialogue between Paxman and CMS regarding appropriate Medicare reimbursement for mechanical scalp cooling. The proposed payment rates under both rules, however, underscore the need for further progress toward fair and reasonable Medicare reimbursement.

In August, Paxman announced a significant regulatory milestone in the development of its Limb Cryocompression System for the reduction of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN), with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) identifying the De Novo process as an appropriate pathway for review of this novel indication. While this development extends Paxman's timeline, the FDA's feedback provides a clear framework for advancing the CIPN programme towards potential U.S. market authorisation and reflects the innovative nature of the technology, which addresses a significant unmet need for cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy.

On September 28th, Paxman announced that California had enacted Assembly Bill 1682, landmark legislation requiring insurance coverage for FDA-cleared scalp cooling systems for cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy, effective from 1 January 2027. As the largest U.S. state to introduce such legislation, California establishes an important benchmark. The new framework is expected to support Paxman’s insurance-based billing model in the U.S. by reducing reimbursement uncertainty, encouraging provider adoption and increasing utilisation of existing systems. California joins five other states with scalp cooling coverage legislation, while additional states are considering similar measures.

After

In late October, Paxman secured its first UK orders for its Neuropathy System ahead of commercial launch. This initial commitment from a major global healthcare group marks a key commercial milestone for Paxman's first expansion beyond scalp cooling into chemotherapy side effect management and an important milestone in the Company's strategy to expand its oncology side effect management portfolio beyond scalp cooling. The four systems will be installed in December 2026.

Paxman announced the official commercial launch of the first-of-its-kind neuropathy system in early November. Scientific evidence highlights a significant unmet need in the management of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN), and the groundbreaking new cryocompression device marks Paxman's first major product expansion beyond scalp cooling – an important milestone in its evolution to Paxman Group.

On November 4th, Paxman announced the publication of phase I/II study data demonstrating safety, tolerability and low rates of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy with the Paxman Neuropathy System. The publication of the latest data from the prospective, multicentre Phase I/II study, evaluating the Paxman Neuropathy System in JCO Oncology Advances marks a significant milestone in the commercialisation pathway of Paxman’s innovative cryocompression technology. The study demonstrated that the device is safe, well tolerated and associated with low rates of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) in patients receiving taxane-based chemotherapy, supporting its potential to address a significant unmet need in cancer care.

Paxman announced on November 13th, that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had successfully completed the acceptance review of the Company's De Novo submission for the Paxman Neuropathy System and has now advanced the application into the substantive review phase. Completion of the acceptance review confirms that the FDA has determined the submission is sufficiently complete for comprehensive scientific and regulatory evaluation. The FDA's target review timeline for a De Novo submission is 150 review days.

About Us

Paxman Group is a global medical technology company focused on improving quality of life for people undergoing chemotherapy through innovative side-effect management solutions. Its portfolio addresses two of the most challenging treatment-related side effects: chemotherapy-induced alopecia (hair loss) and chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN).

Paxman Group’s scalp cooling technologies, including the Paxman Scalp Cooling System and the DigniCap Scalp Cooling System, are used globally in hospitals and cancer centres to support patients undergoing chemotherapy by helping to reduce the risk of chemotherapy-induced hair loss. The clinically validated Paxman Neuropathy System supports the prevention of CIPN through cryocompression technology.

Founded through the Paxman family's personal experience of cancer treatment, Paxman Group works with patients, clinicians and research partners to advance side effect management in cancer care globally.

data.title: European Shares Set To Drift Lower As AI Selloff Deepens
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - European stocks look set to open lower on Friday as AI trade doubts continue to weigh on global technology shares.

U.S. stock futures ticked lower as Anthropic's record listing in New York failed to stem concerns over slower AI infrastructure spending and rising debt loads in the sector.

Anthropic shares fell about 5 percent in extended trade after closing 17 percent above their offer price on their first day of trading.

Asian markets plummeted, with benchmark indexes in Japan and South Korea falling around 5 percent each, amid doubts over whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will translate into profits.

After the release of hawkish Federal Reserve's October policy meeting minutes, investors are also recalibrating their expectations pertaining to upcoming rate decisions.

Speaking at an event on Thursday, Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said stronger economic growth and a labor market at full employment meant inflation should remain the priority for monetary policymakers.

Ahead of the Fed's December meeting, she favored a gradual approach to rate increases, giving the economy time to adjust to higher short-term borrowing costs.

Financial markets have fully priced in a 25-basis point hike at the Fed's December meeting, with a small chance of a super-sized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

The next PCE inflation report is scheduled for release on November 25, with analysts expecting the report to show annual core inflation at 3.2 percent, well above the Fed's 2 percent target.

The U.S. dollar index held near a 19-month high and headed for a fourth weekly gain as AI jitters fueled safe-haven demand.

The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield held near a one-week low on safe-haven bids as investors reassessed equity and AI-related risks.

Gold prices fell nearly 3 percent to $3,527 an ounce in Asian trading and headed for their biggest weekly decline since March as hawkish Fed remarks signaled more interest-rate hikes in the coming months.

Brent crude futures edged up half a percent to $92.52 a barrel but remained on track for a third consecutive weekly decline on signs of abundant global supply.

Overnight, U.S. stocks fluctuated before ending deep in the red as concerns over AI infrastructure spending, semiconductor valuations and the outlook for interest rates overshadowed investor enthusiasm over Anthropic PBC's solid market debut.

Reports warning of risks from chipmaker AMD's ties with Chinese entities and Walmart's disappointing annual sales forecast also weighed on sentiment.

In economic news, labor market data showed first-time claims for unemployment benefits unexpectedly increased slightly last week.

The S&P 500 fell 2 percent to extend losses for a sixth day running and hit a six-month closing low.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 2.3 percent to reach its lowest closing level in seven months while the narrower Dow plummeted 2.2 percent to a six-month low.

European stocks reversed course to end sharply lower on Thursday amid broad-based declines. The pan-European STOXX 600 fell 0.9 percent to extend losses for a fourth consecutive session and reach its lowest level in nearly four weeks.

The German DAX tumbled 1.1 percent, France's CAC 40 fell 0.8 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 dipped 0.9 percent.

data.title: JGB yields track US peers lower; data signals foreign investors lead yield moves
data.description:
By Junko Fujita

Japanese government bond yields fell on Friday, tracking a decline in US Treasury yields overnight, while industry data suggested foreign investors led the sharp declines in JGB yields last month.

The benchmark 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) fell 3 basis points (bps) to 2.79%. The 20-year JGB yield (JP20YTN=JBTC) slid 4 bps to 3.680%. Yields move inversely to bond prices.

JGB yields have tended to track overseas peers in recent sessions as domestic rate-moving cues are limited, with JGB yields having risen high enough to price in the Bank of Japan's future rate hikes, said Masayuki Koguchi, executive chief fund manager at Mitsubishi UFJ Asset Management.

A bigger presence of foreign investors in the market also helped yields move along with those on US Treasuries, he said.

Industry data showed on Friday foreign investors became net buyers of JGBs for a third straight month, buying 3.8 trillion yen worth of JGBs in October, according to data from the Japan Securities Dealers Association, which was compiled by Mizuho Securities.

Foreign investors sold super-long bonds worth 170 billion yen, and bought shorter-dated bonds worth more than 4 trillion yen, the data showed.

"There is a possibility that foreign investors supported sharp declines in JGB yields in October," said Yuki Matsuda, market analyst at Mizuho Securities.

The 10-year bond, which hit a 30-year high of 3.115% in late September, fell to as low as 2.61% in early November.

Global bond yields have declined in the past several weeks as the uncertainty surrounding AI-related stocks has driven safe-haven flows to bonds globally.

On Thursday, US Treasury yields eased as a sharp selloff in US equities pushed investors to buy bonds.

data.title: Gold, silver prices crash today: Muthoot Finance, Hindustan Zinc shares tumble up to 5%; MCX too under pressure
data.description:
Shares of gold loan financiers, including Muthoot Finance, Manappuram Finance and IIFL Finance, tumbled up to 5 percent on Friday, November 20, as international bullion prices crashed further amid expectations of a US Federal Reserve interest-rate hike in December weighed on bullion. Shares of precious metals producer Hindustan Zinc and commodity exchange MCX also witnessed heavy selling as the bullion rout dampened sentiment across metal-linked stocks.

Muthoot Finance shares plunged 5.1 percent to an intra-day low of Rs 2480.10, against its previous close of Rs 2,615 on the BSE. IIFL Finance shares declined 4.7 percent to Rs 614.15 apiece from its previous close of Rs 644.65, while Manappuram Finance shares dropped 4.3 percent to Rs 270.95 apiece, against its previous closing of Rs 283.30.

Shares ofHindustan Zinc fell 4.9 percent to an intraday low of Rs 502.80, against its previous day closing of Rs 528.95. Hindustan Zinc is the largest producer of silver in India, and produces refined silver with a minimum 99.9 percent purity. Hence, the fall in the precious metals pushed the stock down.

Meanwhile, MCX shares also came under pressure, declining 2.8 percent to Rs 3,531.10 apiece, from its previous close of Rs 3,635.

Why are gold loan lender stocks falling?

Non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) such as Muthoot Finance, Manappuram Finance, and IIFL Finance extend loans against gold jewellery, making their lending operations sensitive to volatility in the bullion prices.

A sharp decline in gold prices directly reduces the value of the pledged collateral. Because lenders sanction these loans based on the per-gram rate of gold, borrowers may consequently need to pledge a larger quantity of jewellery to avail the same loan amount, potentially making gold-backed borrowing less attractive and weighing on demand.

Gold, silver prices today

International gold prices fell for a fifth consecutive session on Friday, heading for their steepest weekly decline since March as hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve and a selloff in artificial intelligence-related stocks intensified pressure on bullion.

Spot gold fell 1.9 percent to $3,551.68 per ounce by 0257 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session. Bullion was down about 8.9 percent this week, its sharpest weekly decline since the week of March 20. US gold futures for December delivery slid 3.6 percent to $3,551.90, reported Reuters.

Silver also extended its decline, falling 2.3 percent to $41.98 per ounce after plunging nearly 5 percent in the previous session. The metal has lost around 14 percent during the week.

Among other metals, platinum dropped 2 percent to $1,317.00, and palladium slid 2.3 percent to $888.66. All three metals were headed for weekly losses, Reuters report added.

Why are gold, silver and other metal prices are falling today?

The selloff has been driven by expectations of further US interest-rate hikes as the Federal Reserve maintains a hawkish stance amid persistent inflation. Higher interest rates and bond yields typically weigh on gold by increasing the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding metal.

Bullion has also faced selling pressure amid a rout in technology and AI-related stocks, prompting some investors to liquidate gold holdings to cover losses elsewhere.

"There seems to be a bit of forced liquidation going on across the market in general, with expectations of imminent US rate hikes and inflation that could be persistent, leading to high yields and a higher US dollar as a result, pressuring gold," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, as quoted by Reuters.

MCX gold, silver futures extend sharp losses

Domestic precious metal futures also witnessed heavy selling on Friday. MCX gold futures for December delivery opened 3.94 percent lower at Rs 1,22,430 per 10 grams, while silver futures plunged 5.73 percent to Rs 1,48,466 per kg in early trade.

The latest decline followed Thursday's closing levels of Rs 1,29,380 per 10 grams for gold and Rs 1,61,166 per kg for silver in the domestic market.

data.title: White House names Kirsten Davies as cyber chief after outages hit MSFT, banks
data.description:
The White House appointed a new national cyber director on Thursday, following a series of widespread service disruptions that affected daily life and raised concerns among Americans.

Kirsten Davies, chief information officer at the Defense Department, will fill the role, according to social media posts by several members of Trump's cabinet. She will replace Sean Cairncross as the administration's top cybersecurity official.

“Our nation stands in the crossroad of analog, digital, and quantum technologies, our American way of living increasingly interconnected,” Davies wrote in a post on X. “Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come … but only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on, as well as build cyber talent for our future.”

President Donald Trump faced a groundswell of criticism as Americans grappled with a cascade of service outages that snarled travel, cut off work, limited bank access, and disrupted classified communications.

Even staunch Trump allies accused the administration of lying to Americans or hiding information about the true cause of the disruptions. Over the past week, Microsoft , Chase Bank, air traffic control, and the National Security Agency have all been affected.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday sought to assure Americans that there’s “zero” information that the technical failures are related to each other or to a malign actor.

The White House made the change as Trump returned from a three-day trip to Asia, where he downplayed the episodes, declaring that “things like that happen.”

“She has proven herself to be a dedicated patriot and professional, and we are confident she will advance President Trump’s America First agenda across the cybersecurity landscape,” Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote in a post on X congratulating Davies.

The AP contributed to this report.

data.title: Anthropic's splashy IPO fails to lift AI boat
data.description:
A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Jiaxing Li

Are we nearing the end of the AI boom?

Apparently, even Anthropic's debut as the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company couldn't do much, at least for now, to flip the increasingly worrisome narrative on AI trades.

Its turbulent first day of trading may bode more volatility ahead, with investors beginning to question whether the boom has peaked as the list of positive catalysts thins and exits from crowded trades gather momentum.

MORE POLICY SCRUTINY AHEAD?

This week's blowout earnings from industry bellwether Nvidia were meant to showcase the sector's strong momentum and reignite optimism around the AI trade, but have instead been overshadowed by uncertainty following CEO Jensen Huang's exit.

And as if that chaos was not enough, its powerful rival AMD is now probably next in line for greater US regulatory scrutiny after a short report raised concern about the chipmaker's ties to Chinese entities, some of which have links to firms on US blacklists.

Asian stocks are now feeling the force of the rout, with MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan on track for its worst week since the height of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

That pain now looks set to extend beyond Asia as the day unfolds. In early European trade, pan-region Euro Stoxx 50 futures were down 1.6%. US stock futures also point to further loss, with the S&P 500 e-minis down 0.6%.

DOLLAR, TREASURY CATCH HAVEN FLOW

With risk appetite taking a beating, investors are once again seeking shelter in safer assets.

The US dollar stood near a 19-month peak, bolstered both by risk aversion and growing conviction that the Federal Reserve will raise its key interest rate at its final policy meeting of the year, while Treasury yields also eased on demand for safe government debt.

Key developments that could influence markets on Friday:

  • Anthropic's second-day performance

  • Germany Producer Prices

  • UK Retail Sales

  • UK government debt auctions
